newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo naphtha bearish due to European cargoes.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo naphtha bearish due to European cargoes.

text.p: The Tokyo naphtha market was under pressure on Friday from European cargoes that traders said would be brought into the Asian market for April delivery.
Several Western traders are expected to bring some 150,000 to 200,000 tonnes of European naphtha to Asia for short-covering, market participants said.
Open-spec naphtha for second-half April was assessed at $226.00/228.00 per tonne, down from Thursday's $232.00/233.00.
First-half May was quoted at $222.50/224.50. It was sold from a European trader to a European major at around $228.00 in late Thursday trading, traders said.

Expectations of improved availability also helped shrink the backwardation in naphtha's inter-month spreads, with second-half April/second-half May quoted at plus $4.00/5.00, about $1.00 narrower than Thursday's levels.
The term naphtha price for Kuwaiti cargoes was set at $13.50 per tonne over the mean of Middle Eastern quotes for March 1997 to February 1998, traders said.
The new price compares to the current premium of $7.90 for the one-year term that started last August.
